lines.text: Mara drew maps of places no one had ever seen — until her grandmother's compass pointed somewhere new.
It did not point north. It pointed through the old forest, past the blank edge of every map.
She had drawn a hundred imaginary worlds. She had never once stepped inside one.
The compass grew warm, and the map redrew itself — a stream, a stone, a door of flowers.
So Mara ran — past the meadow, past the last fence, past every reason to turn back.
And there it was: the garden from her grandmother's stories. One compass. One mapmaker. Every scene, the same Mara.
